metadata.note: The San Diego Trolley (Blue, Orange, Green, Copper, and the heritage Silver line), as of the GTFS feed pulled from https://www.sdmts.com/google_transit_files/google_transit.zip. Route geometry, frequency (headway_min, from real scheduled trip counts on a representative Wednesday, Aug 26 2026), and avg_speed_kmh (from real scheduled trip duration) are all sourced directly from the agency's own GTFS feed, same methodology as data/la_metro_rail.geojson and data/rtd_denver_light_rail.geojson. A sixth route in the feed, the 'MTG Event Line' (a special shuttle for Magic: The Gathering conventions at the convention center), was excluded as a temporary event service rather than a permanent line. Historical segments (pre-2026) were added from MTS's own line-opening history: the July 26 1981 South Line (later Blue Line), the first modern light rail built in the US, largely on the old San Diego and Arizona Eastern Railway right-of-way; the 1986 East Line (later Orange Line); the 2005 Green Line; the 2021 Mid-Coast extension to UC San Diego/UTC; and the 2024 Copper Line, the system's newest, which took over the Santee segment from the Orange and Green Lines. Unlike the GTFS-sourced 2026 segment, these older headway numbers are not derived from real historical timetables and should be read as illustrative estimates, not precise data.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.

properties.line: San Diego Metropolitan Transit System: Blue Line

segments.note: The South Line opened July 26 1981 between downtown San Diego and San Ysidro at the Mexican border -- the first modern light rail system built in the United States, running largely over the old San Diego and Arizona Eastern Railway right-of-way. Renamed the Blue Line in 1997. estimated era boundary/frequency based on researched milestone; no historical timetable found, unlike the sourced Amtrak-era frequencies elsewhere in this dataset
